quarterly_data.quarter: Fuji Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (April 2025 - March 2026): net sales JPY 1,227,595 million (109.3% of the prior year) and operating profit JPY 136,620 million (up JPY 18,974 million; 11.1% of net sales). Management states that capital investment in power, manufacturing and data centers stayed firm on GX investment and rising energy demand from wider use of generative AI and digital technology, while US trade policy kept the outlook uncertain and silver and copper prices soared; higher demand for plants and systems, led by Energy, lifted profit despite higher labor costs, raw material costs, lower demand in automotive power semiconductors and the reaction from the prior year's banknote-redesign demand in Food Distribution. Domestic net sales rose 10.6% and overseas net sales 5.9%; the overseas share of net sales was 28.1%.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 1,227,595 million (109.3% of the prior year); operating profit JPY 136,620 million; operating margin 11.1%; overseas share 28.1%

quarterly_data.quarter: Fuji Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Energy segment FY2026 (after the start-of-year reorganisation that moved Facilities Construction into Energy): net sales JPY 394,167 million (FY2025: JPY 354,336 million) and operating profit JPY 59,506 million (FY2025: JPY 36,263 million), mainly on higher demand in Energy Management and Facility and Power Supply Systems. Facility and Power Supply Systems (UPS, switchboards) sales and profit rose on higher demand for data centers; Energy Management rose on more storage battery system projects and more large orders for substation equipment for power and industrial customers and power supply equipment for industrial customers; Power Plants rose on large hydroelectric projects; Facilities Construction rose on large projects and cost reduction. Energy orders received in the year were JPY 3,311 hundred million (Fuji Electric Co., Ltd. Energy segment, non-consolidated basis).
quarterly_data.figure: Energy net sales JPY 394,167 million (FY2025: JPY 354,336 million); operating profit JPY 59,506 million (FY2025: JPY 36,263 million); orders JPY 3,311 hundred million (non-consolidated)

quarterly_data.quarter: Fuji Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductors segment (industrial and automotive power semiconductors) FY2026: net sales JPY 237,386 million (FY2025: JPY 236,788 million) and operating profit JPY 23,520 million (FY2025: JPY 37,081 million, down JPY 13,561 million). Industrial sales rose on higher demand for China and currency effects; automotive sales fell on lower demand for xEV power semiconductors and the prior year's price revisions; profit fell on soaring raw material prices, price competition centred on the Chinese market in industrial, and the automotive demand decline. Orders received JPY 1,877 hundred million (non-consolidated basis).
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductors net sales JPY 237,386 million; operating profit JPY 23,520 million (FY2025: JPY 37,081 million); orders JPY 1,877 hundred million (non-consolidated)

quarterly_data.quarter: Fuji Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Company plan for the year ending March 2027 (April 2026 - March 2027; the company's 'fiscal 2026', the final year of its three-year medium-term plan): net sales JPY 12,750 hundred million, operating profit JPY 1,425 hundred million and net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 1,050 hundred million, aiming to achieve every key indicator (operating margin 11%+, net margin 7%+, ROE 12%+, ROIC 10%+) and record net sales and operating profit. In Energy the company aims to expand orders for UPS, substation equipment and switchboards for data centers and semiconductor plants, where demand is growing sharply, and will invest in production capacity in Japan and overseas to meet strong demand; in Semiconductors it will accelerate development of 8th-generation IGBT and 8-inch SiC and push spec-in activity with global customers for SiC in automotive. Medium-term plan targets for that year: net sales JPY 12,500 hundred million, operating profit JPY 1,400 hundred million (11.2% margin); actual for the year ended March 2026 (the company's 'fiscal 2025'): net sales JPY 12,276 hundred million, operating profit JPY 1,366 hundred million (11.1%). The company will begin formulating its next medium-term plan, starting from its fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: plan for the year ending March 2027: net sales JPY 12,750 hundred million; operating profit JPY 1,425 hundred million; net income JPY 1,050 hundred million; medium-term target net sales JPY 12,500 hundred million, operating margin 11.2%

quarterly_data.quarter: Fuji Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure in FY2026 totalled JPY 56,711 million (Energy JPY 7,965 million; Industry JPY 10,011 million; Semiconductors JPY 34,877 million), for Si and SiC semiconductor capacity, new-product equipment, and capacity expansion and rationalisation at plants in Japan and overseas. In Energy, to meet higher demand for substation equipment driven by more data center and semiconductor plant construction and the replacement of equipment delivered during Japan's high-growth era, the company relocated production equipment from the Chiba Factory to the Kawasaki Factory and invested there to expand switchgear capacity, and began construction of a production-building extension at the Kobe Factory to expand switchboard and power supply equipment capacity. In Semiconductors it invested to raise SiC 6-inch capacity and in 8-inch SiC mass-production technology development.
quarterly_data.figure: capex JPY 56,711 million; Energy JPY 7,965 million; Semiconductors JPY 34,877 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Fuji Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D expenses in FY2026 were JPY 38,907 million (Energy JPY 8,580 million; Industry JPY 12,193 million; Semiconductors JPY 14,168 million). Energy: developed a 300MVA-class large-capacity transformer (275kV in Japan, 230kV overseas) for power infrastructure, about 30% smaller in volume than the previous product (the company calls it world's-smallest class), scheduled for launch during the company's fiscal 2026 (year ending March 2027); launched the '2026 Top Runner' molded transformer (three-phase 20-2,000kVA) with energy efficiency improved 15% across all capacities; developed a 650kVA medium-capacity storage battery PCS and launched a 112.5kW string-type solar PCS; plans to launch in its fiscal 2026 a storage-battery trading operation system that uses AI to optimise electricity market trading.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 38,907 million; Energy R&D JPY 8,580 million; 300MVA transformer about 30% smaller; molded transformer efficiency +15%

quarterly_data.quarter: Fuji Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductors R&D: power modules with 8th-generation IGBT chips are in development, with mass production scheduled to start in the company's fiscal 2026 (year ending March 2027); they cut loss by 15% or more versus same-rated 7th-generation modules and can raise the power density of power electronics equipment such as drives by 10% or more. The company began mass production of a 2,300V/1,200A HPnC module (7th-generation X series chips, insulation raised from 4kV to 6kV) for 1,500V renewable systems and of the 3rd-generation small-capacity IGBT-IPM P641 series; is developing expanded discrete IGBTs (1,200V/140A, 100A; 7th-generation XS chips, TO-247Plus package) for UPS and PCS; and for automotive began mass production of a 750V/600A direct water-cooled module (M682 package, 7th-generation RC-IGBT), is developing a module with 3rd-generation trench-gate SiC MOSFET chips for EV models from 2027 onward with about twice the power density of the M682, and is developing 4th-generation SiC MOSFETs for productisation from the company's fiscal 2030 onward.
quarterly_data.figure: 8th-generation IGBT: loss down 15% or more, power density up 10% or more; HPnC module 2,300V/1,200A; M682 module 750V/600A
